disposition_reason: Field biofortification trial; selenium concentrations are shown only in figures, so only text-stated percentages of the RDA and speciation shares were extracted.

study.design: three-year field fertilization experiment (2012 to 2014) with iodine and selenium (selenate or selenite) soil applications, 1 kg Se/ha
study.method: ICP-OES (Se 169.090 nm) for total selenium; capillary electrophoresis with DAD for selenomethionine

regulatory_or_exposure: Discussion p. 14: authors use RDA of 55 ug selenium/d for adults and 60 to 70 ug/d for pregnant and lactating women
Results p. 9: a 100 g fresh portion of carrot fertilized with selenate would supply 500 to 650% of the adult RDA for selenium; selenite treatments oscillated around or exceeded 100%
Discussion p. 14: control carrots supplied 8.4% (2012) to 41.2% (2014) of the selenium RDA per 100 g
non_numeric_findings: Selenate gave up to several dozen times higher selenium accumulation than selenite (Results p. 8).
Selenomethionine was the dominant measured form; no free selenate or selenite detected in carrot (Discussion).
Share of selenium present as selenomethionine in leaves ranged 18.4% to 96.3% (Results p. 9).
